This claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .1,00,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 14.05.2019 at about 7.15 a.m., he was travelling in Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090 from Sira towards Bengaluru on NH-48 Road, when bus reached over bridge near Indian Overseas Bank, Oorukere Village
, at that time the driver of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-04-MB-1186 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner in a zigzag manner hit to rear end of moving KSRTC Bus.

Due to which, the Car turned turtle and passengers of KSRTC Bus when tried to remove people from the Car, another car bearing Regn.No.MH- 12-MF-0272 driven by its driver from Bengaluru side in a high speed, rash and negligently and in a zigzag manner applied brake and was moving slowly on left side of the road, at that time a Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486 hit to Car bearing Regn.No.MH-12-MF-0272,
due to which, the fish in the Lorry fell on the road and started jumping on the road, at that time the Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 driven by its driver came from Sira side in a high speed in a zigzag manner and observed the fish jumping on the other side of road and slowed down the vehicle,
applied sudden brake neither giving any signal nor observing the movements of other vehicles on the road, the Bus was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the hind portion of Lorry, which was stopped in the middle of the road.
Due to which, he along with other occupants of Bus sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

He was shifted to District Hospital, Tumkuru,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent .1,00,000/- towards treatment and other incidental charges.

Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as a Tailor under Aneena Creations, Peenya Industrial Area, Bengaluru and earning a sum of .12,000/- per month and used to stitch clothes evening at home and thereby earning .10,000/- per month, in all he is earning .20,000/- to .25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanent disablement.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Car, Lorry and Bus by its driver.
The respondents being the Insurers and owners of the offending vehicles are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

19. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discussion one by one.
(i) Towards injury and pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries caused to him,
petitioner has produced wound certificate issued by District Hospital, Tumakuru marked at Ex.P.6, wherein it discloses that the injuries sustained by petitioner are grievous in nature.
So, on perusal of records he took treatment in hospital as an inpatient and the petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.20 & 21.
PW.3/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and he assessed disability for above knee trans tibial amputation at 70%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .60,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced 6 medical bills for .2,303/- marked at Ex.P.13 and 3 medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.14.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .2,303/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 14.05.2019 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Discharge Summary marked at Ex.P.8, issued by District Hospital, Tumakuru,
wherein it shows that petitioner has taken treatment from 14.05.2019 to 01.06.2019 i.e., for a period of 19 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .400/- per day for 19 days to a sum of .7,600/- is just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:

The petitioner has contended that he was working as a Tailor under Aneena Creations, Peenya Industrial Area, Bengaluru and earning a sum of .12,000/- per month and used to stitch clothes evening at home and thereby earning .10,000/- per month, in all he is earning .20,000/- to .25,000/- per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he was earning .20,000/- to .25,000/- per month.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income, this tribunal will consider notional income.

Due to the accidental injuries,
the petitioner might have not attended his regular work at least for a period of 2 months.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2019 at .14,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Principal Benches, Bengaluru.

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka, Principal Benches,
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: So, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to the Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Case on hand the petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove his income.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2019 treated as .14,000/- per month as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .28,000/- (14,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Permanent Disability:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was inpatient at hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, examined as PW.3.
PW.3/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained crush injury to the right lower limb and below knee amputated stump measuring about 3 inches.
The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability for above knee trans tibial amputation at 70%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.20 & 21 documents i.e., clinical report and recent X-ray film.
The petitioner also examined Medical Record Officer as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.15 to 19 i.e., authorization letter, case sheet, MLC Extract, police intimation and 6 X-ray films.
PW.3 in his cross examination deposed that as per hospital documents, there was an amputation below knee and there is 3 inches stump below knee.
Further in his cross examination deposed that the disability given by him at 70% disability.

sentences.text: amputation below knee with stump exceeding 8.89cms, but not exceeding 12.70cms the percentage of loss of earning capacity is 50%.
Amputation below middle thigh to 8.89cms below knee loss of earning capacity is 60%.
Case on hand also doctor has deposed that the petitioner has below knee amputation stump measuring 3 inches from the knee joint (3 inches = 7.62cm).
Hence in the instant case, it is just and proper to consider 60% as working disability.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.

Therefore, considering all these aspects,
the functional disability is assessed at 60%.

In order to prove age of the petitioner, he has produced Ex.P.10 & 11 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card and SSLC Marks Card, wherein the date of birth mentioned as 14.04.1994, the accident occurred on 14.05.2019, so the age of petitioner was 26 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, the same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and multiplier '17' is applicable as per Smt.
Sarla Verma case.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.14,000/- x 12) = .1,68,000/- Loss of future earning p.a. (60% of prior annual income) .1,00,800/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 17 Loss of future earnings - (.1,00,800/- x 17) = .17,13,600/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .17,13,600/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day-today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .50,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.3 has opined that the petitioner needs a below knee Prosthesis, the estimate of this prosthesis is around .5,00,000/- and also need regular maintenance, which is around .10,000/- and change of socket once in five year.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 - Estimate, wherein mentioned that the total cost which includes socket measurements, fabrication, trails, gait training and fixation of final prosthesis is .5,25,000/- and maintenance cost of artificial prosthesis every year will be around .10,000/-.
